children: Mass market automakers gaining ground in the premium segment; Merc, BMW work out different strategies to drive growth Lijee Philip Mumbai: India's luxury car sales volume remains stuck at around 1% of the passenger vehicle market, as affluent buyers look beyond the traditional marquee brands.

The top end of the market has become crowded, with automakers that do not traditionally carry a luxury tag such as Toyota, Kia, MG and BYD bringing high-priced premium models and taking away a section of potential customers who would have otherwise chosen the likes of Mercedes-Benz, Audi or BMW. Data collated by automobile consultancy Jato Dynamics show a marginal fall in the market share of legacy luxury automakers so far in calendar 2026, to 0.98% from 1.1% in 2025, even as the premium model range of mainstream and new-age brands grew their share to 0.14% from 0.12%. The traditional luxury brands are now pursuing different routes for growth.

Mercedes-Benz is moving further up the price ladder, while BMW is looking to widen the luxury offering with more products, electric vehicles, localisation and customers upgrading from mainstream brands, said their executives. Mercedes-Benz India is targeting growth in value market share.

Its average selling price has increased to about 1 crore over the past couple of years from around 60 lakh. "We should not be looking at luxury growth from the prism of absolute volume and penetration alone, but from the quality of sales and value it adds," said Santosh Iyer, managing director and CEO at the Indian unit of the German automaker. Its top-end portfolio grew 20% in the first half of 2026 and accounts for 30% of sales. The company said it is seeing an increasing number of younger, first-time buyers. BMW is targeting expansion from another direction.

title: Legacy Luxury Car Brands Get Run for their Money
